title: The paper road
note: How Greek and Indian learning reached Europe through Arabic.

research.quotes: heroes.html#f-word-and-page: 'Between the eighth and tenth centuries, Baghdad paid fortunes to move the mind of the ancient world into Arabic.' 'The greatest of the translators, Hunayn ibn Ishaq, was an Arab Christian who hunted manuscripts across the Near East and translated for meaning rather than word by word.' 'the translators' heirs did something better: they argued back. Ptolemy's star positions were remeasured and corrected.' 'When Europe grew hungry in the twelfth century, it came to Toledo and translated the Arabic, corrections, commentaries, and all; Gerard of Cremona alone carried some seventy works into Latin.' 'not as a sealed box passed hand to hand but as a working library, used hard and improved.'
research.retell: Long ago, scholars in Baghdad translated Greek science into Arabic and even corrected mistakes in it, and later translators in Spain carried that improved knowledge into Latin, which is how it reached the science books people use today.

lines.text: Your science passed through Arabic first
lines.sub: even math and medicine came this way

lines.text: He hunts down rare Greek manuscripts
He translates meaning, not each word
Toledo then translates his Arabic work
Then Europe teaches from his translation
This was correction, not mere copying
Your textbook still carries his work
lines.sub: it was carried carefully, and improved

lines.text: Handing a thing on is its own glory
